## Module 4 in two minutes

**Three columns — time, headcount, budget — and one rule: each comes from an artifact, not from recall.** Self-report on time allocation is unreliable in a flattering direction. It understates Produce, because drafting is unglamorous, and overstates Decide, because Decide is what we'd like to be doing.

**Every instrument has a known distortion.** Calendars over-count Decide and Distribute and miss drafting entirely. Task trackers miss counsel, because "told the CFO the framing was wrong" is not a ticket. The Module 1 send audit is complete for Produce and Distribute and silent on the other four. A five-day reconstruction is perfectly acceptable **if you label it as one** and write it day by day.

**And if you lead a team, map the team.** A director's week is mostly Decide, so mapping yourself will show a healthy function sitting on top of four people doing nothing but Produce.

### The rule to carry

**Ownership is the question whose only acceptable answer is a person's name:** *if this link fails, whose performance review does it appear in?* Touching a link is not owning it. Sense and Verify usually have nobody — and **work that appears in nobody's review is work that stops happening the first busy month.**

The two corrections that move every map: **proofreading is Produce, not Verify** (Verify asks whether it was true and whether it landed), and **a meeting that changed what gets said is Decide, not Produce**, however many drafts were on screen.

**The full module adds** the four function shapes and their prescriptions — the production shop starts with Verify rather than Sense because it's cheaper and protects existing output; the broadcast desk already owns its listening instrument and isn't reading it — plus the gap that matters most: **time in Produce, money in Distribute**, so the largest financial lever points at the link that was already solved, with no budget line at all against the two links AI just opened. That sentence with your own numbers in it is the strongest line in your Module 10 proposal. The four-map exercise trains reading a map rather than drawing one.
